cohort: The study included 1663 women with singleton pregnancies following IVF-ICSI (study group) and 3326 women with singleton spontaneous pregnancies (control group), matched 1:2 by age, BMI, parity, and gravidity, who delivered between January 2015 and January 2018 at the Peking University Third Hospital.
finding: IVF-ICSI is associated with an increased risk of obstetric complications, including preterm delivery, gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders, and placenta previa, in singleton pregnancies compared to spontaneous pregnancies.
gest_age: Deliveries before 28, 32, and 34 weeks gestation were considered preterm.
